source_caption:
One of the most fascinating and unconventional sports biopics ever made. I, Tonya tells the story of figure skater Tonya Harding, exploring her rise to fame, troubled upbringing, and the scandal that changed her life forever. What makes the film so compelling is how it moves beyond the headlines to show the complicated people behind one of the most infamous moments in sports history.

Margot Robbie is phenomenal as Tonya, but Allison Janney is equally unforgettable as her mother, LaVona. Interestingly, Janney had trained as a figure skater throughout her childhood before a serious leg injury at 17 forced her to stop. She went on to win an Oscar for a role she filmed in just eight days. Her performance is a masterclass in making an incredibly difficult character impossible to forget.

🎥: I, Tonya (2017)
Dir. Craig Gillespie

source_details.title: I, Tonya
source_details.synopsis: I, Tonya is a 2017 biographical comedy-drama sports film directed by Craig Gillespie and written by Steven Rogers. It follows the life and career of American figure skater Tonya Harding and her connection to the 1994 assault on her rival Nancy Kerrigan. The film states it is based on "contradictory" and "totally true" interviews with Harding and her ex-husband Jeff Gillooly, suggesting they are unreliable narrators. It features darkly comedic interviews with the characters, set in the modern day, and breaks the fourth wall. Margot Robbie (who also produced) stars as Harding, Sebastian Stan as Gillooly, and Allison Janney as Harding's mother LaVona Golden. Julianne Nicholson, Caitlin Carver,
